$comment: The OpenAct Promptbook: the design system for OpenAct apps. People and coding agents read this file before they draw a screen. Token values live in theme.css. `npm run design -- check` tests this file against theme.css and the app code. `npm run design -- build` publishes it to https://openact.ing/design.
name: OpenAct Promptbook
premise: In a theater, the prompt book is the stage manager's master copy of the show. It holds the script, every cue and every move. The crew works from it. The Promptbook does the same job for OpenAct apps. It holds the tokens, the rules and the checks in one place. Agents read it first. People approve what the agents make.

principles.title: Written for agents first
principles.text: The source is a JSON file and a Markdown file, not a picture. An agent can read every rule. A person can read every rule too.

principles.title: Intent, not values
principles.text: Pick a token by what it means. Use status-done for a done task. Never pick a green because it looks good. The values can change. The meaning stays.

principles.title: Seeds, not palettes
principles.text: A new app gives one seed: a hue. The design script makes the light and dark values and tests their contrast. Agents do not invent palettes.

principles.title: Agents have their own states
principles.text: Agent work has five states: think, act, wait, done and fail. Each state has its own token and icon. A person can always see what the agent does.

principles.title: Every rule has a check
principles.text: A rule is a cue. Each cue has a check: a script, a test or a review by a person. The script runs with the unit tests.

surface.intent: The planes that content sits on.

items.card: A raised panel, such as a task card or a dialog.
items.muted: A quiet fill, such as a hover row or a code chip.
items.muted-foreground: Secondary text: dates, help text, counts.
items.input: The edge of a form field.
items.scrim: The shade behind a dialog or a sheet.

items.primary: The main action on a screen. Use one per screen.
items.accent-foreground: Text on a hover or selected state.
items.destructive: An action that deletes or cannot be undone.

brand.intent: The OpenAct identity: Playbill ink with a stage gold cue.

items.brand: The ink of the OpenAct mark.
items.brand-gold: The cue light. Use it for brand moments only, never for status.

meaning.intent: Colors that carry meaning. Never use them for decoration.

items.live: Something changes now, such as another viewer on the page.
items.today: The line for today on a timeline.

agent.intent: The five states of agent work. They never use the brand colors.

items.agent-wait: The agent needs a person to approve or reject.
items.agent-fail: The step failed or a person rejected it.

stage.intent: Fixed surfaces that look the same in both themes.

items.paper: A Docs page. It stays light, like printed paper.
items.desk: The area around a Docs page.

identity.intent: Colors that tell items apart. They have no meaning of their own.

items.av-0: Avatar color, picked from the person's id.

classes.$comment: Tailwind classes for tokens whose class name is not the token name.

contrast.$comment: Pairs that the check tests in light and dark. text needs 4.5:1. graphic needs 3:1.

agentStates.label: Reading
agentStates.rule: Show what the agent reads, such as "Reading 12 tasks". Pulse slowly. Stop the pulse for reduced motion.

agentStates.label: Running
agentStates.rule: Name the tool in plain words, such as "Moving 3 tasks". Show one step at a time.

agentStates.label: Waiting for you
agentStates.rule: Show the change in plain words with Approve and Reject buttons. Deletes and people changes always wait. The agent never goes past this state on its own.

agentStates.label: Done
agentStates.rule: Say what changed. Link to the changed item when you can.

agentStates.label: Stopped
agentStates.rule: Say what went wrong and what to do next.

shape.use: Use rounded-md for controls, rounded-lg for cards and rounded-full for avatars and pills.

motion.use: Enter with ease-enter. Leave with ease-exit, faster than the enter. Reorder and drag with ease-move. Every animation stops for prefers-reduced-motion.

blocking.use: A list of items and the open item.
A chat with the agent beside the work.

cues.rule: Use theme tokens for every color. Do not write hex, rgb or oklch values or fixed Tailwind palette classes in components.
Give every token a light value and a dark value.
Text has a contrast of 4.5:1 or more on its surface, in both themes.
Status marks, icons and lines that carry meaning have a contrast of 3:1 or more.
Pick a token by its intent. Do not pick a token by its color.
Use one primary action on a screen.
Every signed-in page starts with SiteHeader and puts its content in PageBody.
Build from the @openact/ui components: Arc first, then shadcn/ui. Build a new component in @openact/ui only when neither has one. Use Lucide icons through Icon.
Show agent work with the five agent states and the AgentState component. Never show agent work in the brand colors.
An agent change that deletes data or changes people waits for a person. Show Approve and Reject.
Use the motion tokens. Stop every animation when the person asks for reduced motion.
Write text in ASD-STE100 style: short sentences, active voice, one idea per sentence, American spelling.
Do not use em dashes in text.
Start the name of an app token with the app id, such as --app-docs-accent.
Look at every new screen in light and dark, on a phone and on a desktop, before you open a pull request.

method.name: Script
method.person: Write one sentence about who uses the app and what they do.
method.agent: Read the Promptbook. Pick the blocking pattern for each screen.

method.name: Cast
method.person: Pick one hue for the app accent, if the app needs one.
method.agent: Run npm run design -- seed <app-id> <hue>. Paste the tokens into theme.css.

method.name: Block
method.agent: Build each screen from the blocking pattern and @openact/ui components.

method.name: Cue
method.person: Say which agent actions need approval.
method.agent: Show agent work with AgentState. Write all text in ASD-STE100 style.

method.name: Rehearse
method.person: Look at the screens in light and dark, on a phone and a desktop.
method.agent: Run npm run design -- check and npm test. Fix every problem.

method.name: Open
method.person: Review the pull request and merge it.
method.agent: Open a pull request. List the cues that need a review by a person.
